video.title: Facebook Founder Mark Zuckerberg Commencement Address | Harvard Commencement 2017

motivational.video_read: Mark Zuckerberg's 2017 Harvard commencement address, delivered live with applause throughout — there is no cold-open montage, the speech starts at line 1. The material that works on a 2am viewer is not the civic 'purpose for everyone' thesis but three pockets of personal, identity-level material: the innovation run in the middle (ideas don't come out fully formed, the Eureka lie, being misunderstood, feeling like an impostor at 22), the 'they're not — you will' turn after the Facebook founding story, and the undocumented student story near the close. The rest is graduation-ceremony inspiration aimed at a graduating class, not at the person scrolling alone.

near_misses.why_not: The second landing of the student story ('if a high school senior who doesn't know what the future holds can do his part, we owe it to the world') needs the story before it — 'I can't even say his name' dangles for a stranger, and the combined run exceeds a reel-sized minute.
A list of generational projects (climate, curing disease, online voting) — inspiring at a graduation, but the viewer can pick up nothing about themselves from it.
Rowling's twelve rejections and Beyoncé's hundreds of songs are other people's résumés; 'the greatest successes come from the freedom to fail' is the only takeaway and it arrives generic.
An honest argument about luck, loans and safety nets, but it is policy aimed at the system — it leaves the broke viewer holding the problem rather than something to stand on.
The janitor-at-NASA story and the 'create a world where everyone has purpose' thesis are warm and famous, but they read as civic mission for graduates — the viewer nods instead of replaying.
The closing prayer and 'may your life be a blessing' is a gentle outro — comfort placed without any evidence or turn before it.

skipped.what: live intro, thanks, and joke anecdotes (inside-out T-shirt, Facemash, meeting Priscilla) — charming, not motivation
great-projects-of-past-generations build-up into the dam setup
transition recaps of the three-part speech structure
UBI, child care, charity and the after-school teaching story — policy and gratitude, no identity hit
global community vs nationalism — the 'struggle of our time' passage is political, not personal
community examples (Agnes, Kayla, David) and 'change starts local' — profile of others, no takeaway

clips.title: Let me tell you a secret: no one knows what they're doing when they begin
clips.why: Removes the exact excuse the scared viewer is holding — 'I don't know how, so I can't start.' He voices the viewer's own thought ('I don't know how to build a dam'), then kills it with 'no one does when they begin' and lands it on himself: had he needed to know everything first, Facebook would never exist. Note: the final word 'Facebook' is the first word of L0090 — cut there.

clips.title: He has every reason to be cynical — and he wasn't feeling sorry for himself
clips.why: A story that detonates: an undocumented teenager who may be denied his dream, asked what he wants for his birthday, asks for a book on social justice. The build is real and the payoff reframes the viewer's own self-pity — someone with far less was still looking outward. Heavily replayed by viewers. The leading word 'Club' is the tail of the previous sentence; cut to 'one day after class'. L0214–L0216 ('maybe you're asking yourself, can I really do this') sits just before and could serve as a lifted hook.

clips.end_words: and he's going to bring people along with him
clips.text: Club one day after class I was talking to my students about going to college and one of my top students raised his hand and said that he wasn't sure he could go to college because he's undocumented Ed he wasn't sure if they'd take him last year I took him out to breakfast for his birthday and I wanted to get him a gift so I asked him what he wanted and he just started talking about struggles that he saw other students in his class facing and finally said you know I'd really just like a book on social justice I was blown away here is a young guy who has every reason to be cynical he wasn't sure if the country he calls home the only one he's known was going to deny him his dream of going to college but he wasn't feeling sorry for himself he wasn't even thinking of himself he has a greater sense of purpose and he's going to bring people along with him

clips.title: You're sure someone else is going to do it — but they're not. You will.
clips.why: The build — kids in a dorm assuming a big company would connect the world — sets up one of the cleanest identity handovers in the speech: the thing you're waiting for someone else to do is yours. 'But they're not. You will.' is the landing; cut there, because the rest of L0069 ('it's not enough to have that purpose yourself...') opens a different thought that doesn't pay off inside this clip.
clips.start_words: I remember that night I launched Facebook
clips.text: I remember that night I launched Facebook from that little dorm in Kirkland house I went to noes with my friend KX and I remember telling him clearly that I was excited to help connect the Harvard Community but one day someone would connect the whole world the thing is it never even occurred to me that that someone might be us we were just college kids we didn't know anything about that there were all these great big technology companies with all these resources and I just assumed one of them would do it but this idea was so clear to us that all people want to connect so we just kept working on it day after day after day and I know that a lot of you are going to have your own stories just like this a change in the world that seems so clear that you are sure someone else is going to do it but they're not you will but it's not enough to have that purpose yourself you also have to create a sense of purpose for others and I found that out the hard

clips.title: The idea of a single Eureka moment is a dangerous lie
clips.why: Names a private wound the viewer has never heard said: they feel inadequate because their eureka moment hasn't arrived yet — and says the moment itself is a lie invented by movies. That reorganises how they read their own 'lateness'. End the reel on 'getting started in the first place'; the math-formulas joke after it is a different register and should be dropped.

clips.title: An impostor — a 22-year-old kid who had no idea how things actually worked
clips.why: Zuckerberg, with nothing to gain from admitting it, describes the exact 2am feeling: everyone left, everyone wanted to sell, 'I felt alone and worse, it was my fault. I wondered if I was just wrong — an impostor, a 22-year-old kid.' The turn — 'now years later I understand, that is how things work' — converts the doubt from proof of inadequacy into proof of being in the game. Runs long; the second pass can start at L0075 ('if I didn't agree to sell the company right now...') for a tighter cut. The leading word 'world' is a caption fragment from the previous sentence.

clips.end_words: when there's no sense of higher purpose
clips.text: world nearly everyone else wanted to sell without a sense of higher purpose this was their startup dream come true and it tore our company apart after one particularly tense argument one of my close advis told me if I didn't agree to sell the company right now I would regret that decision for the rest of my life relationships were so Fray that within a year or so every single person on our management team was gone that was my hardest time leading Facebook I believed in what we were doing but I felt alone and worse it was my fault I wondered if I was just wrong an impostor a a 22-year-old kid who had no idea how things actually worked now years later I understand that is how things work when there's no sense of higher purpose so it's up to all of us to create it so we can all keep moving forward

clips.title: Be prepared to be misunderstood
clips.why: Reframes the criticism the ambitious viewer is already living with — called crazy, blamed for not understanding, criticized for moving too fast — as the fixed price of taking on anything big, not a verdict on them. Ends on 'that can't stop us from getting started' (the word 'started' opens L0099 — cut there). It is list-shaped in the middle, which is why it ranks below the sharper single-idea clips.

clips.title: No one knows when they begin — and the Eureka moment is a lie (both together)
clips.why: The two preceding landings run straight into each other as one continuous run of speech ('...I never would have built Facebook. Movies and pop culture just get this all wrong...') — returned as a pair as well, for an editor who wants the full build. End on 'getting started in the first place'; the final word 'Facebook' of the first landing sits at the top of L0090 and the math-formulas joke at the tail of L0091 should both be trimmed.
